summary_en.motivation: This study aims to improve the mechanical properties of Ti-6Al-4V alloy by heavy warm rolling of an acicular martensitic microstructure.
summary_en.method: Heavy warm rolling was applied to a martensitic starting microstructure to achieve grain refinement and homogeneity.
summary_en.result: The warm rolling process resulted in improved strength and ductility due to microstructure homogenization.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical properties were validated by tensile testing and microstructure analysis.

papers.title: NUMERICAL MODELING OF MECHANICAL MACHINING OF TITANIUM ALLOYS: ANALYSIS OF HEAT FIELD, SHEAR FORCES AND CUTTING TOOL WEAR
papers.abstract: Due to their important properties such as high strength, low density, and high corrosion resistance, titanium alloys are widely used for the aerospace industry. The importance of titanium alloys is enormous, especially in the manufacture of structural elements, engine parts, and responsible parts with high loads. Besides the positive aspects of these materials, however, there are also a number of problems with their mechanical treatment. In particular, the low thermal transfer of titanium alloys leads to the accumulation of heat generated during cutting in the shear zone, which makes the machining process significantly more difficult. In this study, the mechanical machining process of Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy was investigated using numerical modeling techniques. Simulations were carried out on the SimScale platform, where heat dissipation during cutting, the distribution of Von Mises voltages and the process of bending of the cutting tool were analyzed in detail. The results of the calculation showed that all the bulk of the heat generated during the cutting process is concentrated exactly in the cutting zone and does not dissipate rapidly enough throughout the material. It was also found that maximum Von Mises voltages occur in the contact region between the cutting tool and the part being machined. It has been observed that these high voltages and intense heat flux cause rapid erosion of the instrument, especially in the area of the steep edge. As a result, the service life of the cutting tool is shortened and the processing quality may deteriorate. The results of the obtained modeling have important application for the optimization of the machining process, the correct selection of cutting modes and increase the tool resource, and serve to increase the efficiency of machining titanium alloys.
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

summary_zh.motivation: 研究钛合金机械加工中热场和刀具磨损问题
summary_zh.method: 使用SimScale平台进行数值模拟，分析切削过程中热分布和应力
summary_zh.result: 发现热量集中在切削区，最大应力出现在刀具与工件接触区，导致刀具磨损
summary_zh.validation: 纯数值模拟，无实验验证

summary_en.motivation: To investigate heat accumulation and tool wear during machining of titanium alloys due to low thermal conductivity.
summary_en.method: Numerical simulations on SimScale platform analyzing heat dissipation, von Mises stresses, and tool bending during Ti-6Al-4V cutting.
summary_en.result: Heat concentrates in the shear zone, peak stresses occur at the tool-workpiece interface, causing rapid tool wear and reduced tool life.
summary_en.validation: The study relies solely on numerical simulations without experimental validation.

summary_zh.motivation: 分析钛合金机械加工中的热场和力分布，优化切削工艺。
summary_zh.method: 在SimScale平台上对Ti-6Al-4V切削进行数值模拟。
summary_zh.result: 切削热集中在剪切区，最大等效应力出现在刀具与工件接触区，导致刀具磨损。
summary_zh.validation: 纯数值模拟，无实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: The study aims to analyze heat dissipation, shear forces, and tool wear during mechanical machining of Ti-6Al-4V to optimize cutting parameters.
summary_en.method: Numerical simulations were performed on the SimScale platform to model the machining process of Ti-6Al-4V, focusing on temperature distribution, von Mises stress, and tool deformation.
summary_en.result: Heat generated during cutting concentrates in the shear zone without rapid dissipation, and maximum von Mises stresses occur at the tool-workpiece interface, leading to accelerated tool wear.
summary_en.validation: The study is purely numerical with no experimental validation; results are based on simulation case studies.
